title: Solenoid Valve

introduction.definition: A solenoid valve is an electrically operated on/off valve. Current in the coil creates a magnetic field that lifts a plunger. In the pilot-operated (servo) type modelled, the plunger opens a small pilot orifice; the pressure above the diaphragm bleeds to the outlet and line pressure lifts the diaphragm off the main seat. When the coil is switched off the spring closes the pilot and the diaphragm reseats.
applications: Water, air and gas shut-off in automation
key_points: Pilot-operated needs a minimum ΔP; direct-acting does not
Coil voltage and duty must match
introduction.summary: A solenoid valve opens and closes electrically. In this normally-closed, pilot-operated design the coil lifts a small plunger, which opens a pilot orifice; pressure above the diaphragm bleeds away and line pressure lifts the diaphragm off the main seat. De-energising the coil lets the spring push the plunger back and the valve closes. A minimum pressure difference is needed to operate.

steps.text: De-energised: the spring holds the plunger on the pilot orifice; inlet pressure above the diaphragm keeps it closed.
Energised: the coil field pulls the plunger up.
The pilot orifice opens; cover pressure escapes to the outlet faster than the bleed hole refills it.
Line pressure lifts the diaphragm and flow passes the main orifice.
De-energising lets the plunger drop; pressure builds above the diaphragm and the valve closes.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: On/off device; response time from tens of milliseconds (direct) to ~1 s (large pilot valves).

magnetic_field.title: Magnetic field
magnetic_field.description: When the coil is energised its magnetic field (loops) is concentrated by the plunger and pulls it up, opening the pilot orifice. Cover pressure then bleeds to the outlet, so line pressure lifts the diaphragm and the main orifice opens.

annotations.text: Coil energised → field pulls plunger up

foundation: Support the valve and adjoining pipe so the body does not carry pipe weight or thermal loads; heavy valves need their own supports.
alignment: Align flanges face-to-face and bore-to-bore before bolting; never pull pipes into place with the bolts.
Respect the flow-direction arrow on the body.
piping: Fit a strainer upstream — dirt blocks the bleed and pilot orifices.
Install with the coil upward where recommended.
commissioning: Check the valve strokes fully and smoothly.
Pressure-test the line (shell test) with the valve partly open; do not use the valve to blind a test above its seat rating.
Record the as-installed position and set points.

periodic.task: Clean diaphragm, bleed and pilot orifices.

overhaul.task: Replace diaphragm, plunger seal and spring with a repair kit.

lubrication: None — do not oil the plunger tube.

remedies: Check ΔP, coil resistance, clean pilot

causes: Blocked bleed hole, torn diaphragm, dirt on seat

script.narration: This module introduces the Solenoid Valve.
A solenoid valve is an electrically operated on/off valve.
Current in the coil creates a magnetic field that lifts a plunger.
In the pilot-operated (servo) type modelled, the plunger opens a small pilot orifice; the pressure above the diaphragm bleeds to the outlet and line pressure lifts the diaphragm off the main seat.
Typical applications include water, air and gas shut-off in automation; burner fuel shut-off (safety shut-off valves); cooling water and process utilities; pneumatic control circuits.

script.narration: How the Solenoid Valve works.
De-energised: the spring holds the plunger on the pilot orifice; inlet pressure above the diaphragm keeps it closed.
Energised: the coil field pulls the plunger up.
The pilot orifice opens; cover pressure escapes to the outlet faster than the bleed hole refills it.
Line pressure lifts the diaphragm and flow passes the main orifice.
De-energising lets the plunger drop; pressure builds above the diaphragm and the valve closes.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
When the coil is energised its magnetic field (loops) is concentrated by the plunger and pulls it up, opening the pilot orifice.

video_tutorials.title: Solenoid Valve — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Solenoid Valve.
Check coil temperature and operation.
Clean diaphragm, bleed and pilot orifices.
Replace diaphragm, plunger seal and spring with a repair kit.
Watch for valve does not open: coil energised, no flow. Common cause: ΔP below minimum.
Watch for valve does not close: flow continues. Common cause: blocked bleed hole, torn diaphragm, dirt on seat.
Watch for coil burn-out: coil open-circuit, smell. Common cause: wrong voltage, stuck plunger (AC).
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.

questions.question: Why does a pilot-operated solenoid valve need a minimum pressure difference?
options: Line pressure is what lifts the diaphragm

questions.question: A common cause of AC coil burn-out is…
options: Plunger stuck so the coil draws high inrush current
questions.explanation: AC coil current falls only when the plunger closes the magnetic circuit.
